note: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 180df07922 (Resolve returns *yang.Resolved, one Resolve per Loader; process, checkExtensions, checkPatterns, checkStructure still all run and join, refusals unchanged): only the ModuleLoadAccepted tail changed. RFC 7.19: 'the substatements MUST be YANG statements, including extensions defined using "extension" statements.' The earlier finding that sources was keyed by file name no longer holds at HEAD: sourcedModules.texts is keyed by *yang.Module (Parse binds each module added by a parse to its text). Revert records on AddModuleFromText for the ModuleLoadAccepted/Refused tags are owed a re-record. Prior judgement, still true: Re-judged 2026-10-09 after 6c06cb43af/037cc25e29. Sentence 1: TestRFC7950ExtensionUsageSubstatementsAreYANGStatements refuses m:e "x" { bogus "y"; } against description and nested m:e twins. Sentence 2 (Section 14 rules) now whole: substatements are resolved against the embedded RFC ABNF (resolveProduction) and checked for argument grammar (config maybe, namespace not a URI, path a / ../a[), cardinality (two type, two description; one type + two must loads), required substatements and blocks (leaf without type, list without data-def, refine with no block) and context forms (deviate add/not-supported mixing, type-body alternatives, augment absolute vs descendant), each tagged test with a revert record on its producer. Independent probe 2026-10-09 of ~70 valid unusual forms under a usage (quoted/unquoted/single-quoted args, + concatenation, nested usages at depth, leafref require-instance, multiple leaf-list defaults, deviate add/replace/delete in full, if-feature expressions with extra whitespace, path predicates with WSP, IPv6/percent URIs, refine across comments/newlines/tabs/UTF-8/CRLF, nested module/submodule) all load; config TRUE, max-elements 0/007, fraction-digits 19, deref() path, refine x; via comment or concatenation, empty input/augment are refused. The ModuleLoadRefused/Accepted tags drive the extension DEFINITION (extension e { bogus }), governed by the Section 14 extension-stmt rule, a neighbouring rule; their claims state what the body checks but do not bear on this sentence.
